description: Short, auditable takeaways extracted from public VLA repositories. These are decision rules for the research router, not copied trajectory data.

projects.name: OpenVLA
facts: OpenVLA accepts arbitrary mixtures of RLDS datasets and supports Open X-Embodiment mixtures.
Its action prediction path must use the matching dataset unnormalization key before robot execution.
The repository provides LoRA, partial and full fine-tuning paths, plus a REST serving path.
The released 7B model was trained on a large Open X-Embodiment mixture and is evaluated on BridgeData V2 and LIBERO workflows.
decisions: keep an RLDS manifest
verify action statistics and unnormalization key
separate simulation and real-robot evaluation

projects.name: LeRobot
facts: The standard dataset flow records synchronized video together with action and robot state, plus a task instruction.
The same dataset contract is used by recording, training, evaluation and deployment tools.
A custom policy should expose configuration, model and pre/post processors so it can run through the common train/eval/rollout commands.
Reported benchmark results should include the suite, success rate, episode count, hardware and a reproducible evaluation command.
decisions: repair missing observation.state or task fields before training
keep train/eval/rollout processors identical
report episode counts with success rate

projects.name: RoboTwin 2.0
facts: RoboTwin 2.0 is a dual-arm manipulation data generator and benchmark with strong domain randomization.
The repository releases more than 100,000 pre-collected trajectories but recommends collecting with the chosen task and embodiment configuration.
Its research axes include single-task fine-tuning, visual robustness, language diversity, multi-task capability and cross-embodiment performance.
The platform distinguishes clean and randomized evaluation phases and reports task-level results.
decisions: keep clean and randomized evaluation separate
record task and embodiment config with every trajectory
test visual, language and embodiment shifts independently

projects.name: LIBERO
facts: LIBERO provides 130 tasks in Spatial, Object, Goal and LIBERO-100 suites with controlled and entangled distribution shifts.
LIBERO-100 is split into LIBERO-90 for policy pretraining and LIBERO-10 for downstream lifelong-learning testing.
The repository supports separate training and evaluation scripts when GPU resources are limited.
The benchmark focuses on knowledge transfer and reports learning and success behavior over task sequences, not one pooled random split.
decisions: hold out the downstream suite before training
choose a suite that matches the claimed transfer axis
preserve task order and seed in the evaluation manifest

projects.name: Octo
facts: Octo is pretrained on a diverse mixture of about 800,000 robot trajectories from Open X-Embodiment.
It supports language or goal-image conditioning, multiple cameras, observation history and different action spaces.
The repository exposes head-only, head-plus-MLP and full fine-tuning modes for adapting a new robot setup.
The published adaptation studies use small target-domain datasets and test new observations, actions and embodiments.
decisions: start with a small adaptation mode when target data is limited
declare the new observation and action spaces
compare against training from scratch

projects.name: openpi / Pi0
facts: The repository contains flow-based Pi0 and autoregressive Pi0-FAST models pretrained on more than 10,000 hours of robot data.
The README estimates more than 22.5 GB for LoRA fine-tuning and more than 70 GB for full fine-tuning on a single GPU.
The training configs use LeRobot-style data and expose worker, device and batch settings.
Normalization statistics should be consciously reloaded or recomputed on the target data and compared in an experiment.
decisions: select LoRA when the GPU budget cannot hold full fine-tuning
record the normalization-statistics choice
keep an explicit target-data config

projects.name: Open X-Embodiment
facts: Open X-Embodiment standardizes many robot datasets as RLDS episode sequences.
Its basic RT-X observation path pairs an RGB workspace image with a task string.
The collection spans many robots, skills and institutions, so robot embodiment and label coverage must be retained in metadata.
A mixture is useful only when observation, action and language fields are mapped consistently.
decisions: keep source and embodiment identifiers
audit missing language and sensor fields before mixing
evaluate cross-embodiment transfer separately
